authors: Z. Bern, J. Parra-Martinez, R. Roiban
title: Cancelling the U(1) anomaly in the S-matrix of N=4 supergravity
claim: At one loop, the U(1)-anomalous N=4 supergravity amplitudes (violating a tree-level charge-conservation rule) can be set to zero by adding a finite local counterterm; the same counterterm cancels evanescent contributions relevant to UV analyses in dimensionally regularized gravity. The previously reported four-loop divergence was obtained without this counterterm and needs reanalysis.
scheme: Dimensional regularization (variant not stated in the abstract).
symmetry_argument: Symmetry restoration by a finite local counterterm (structurally analogous to BMHV-type symmetry-restoring counterterms); evanescent operators and anomaly 'tightly intertwined' (1706.01486).

proved: One-loop: a finite local counterterm removes the anomalous amplitudes and the evanescent pieces (abstract).
checked_partially: Effect on the four-loop divergence left open.

evidence: Abstract; companion 1706.01486 (Bern-Edison-Kosower-Parra-Martinez, PRD 96 (2017) 066004): D-dim one-loop amplitudes via double copy, evanescent curvature-squared multiplets intertwined with U(1)-anomalous contributions.
red_flags: Direct example where a DR loop result (four-loop divergence) is contaminated by an evanescent/anomalous sector that a finite counterterm can change: a DR UV statement need not be scheme-independent physics until the symmetry-restoring finite counterterms are fixed.
cross_checks: S1d.08_BDDSS2013; 1507.06118 (S1d.11_BCCDDN2015) for evanescent effects in pure gravity.
notes: Not in the brief's lead list; added because it is a DR + anomaly + finite-counterterm example in a supersymmetric theory.
